No audio - Because it is an extract of the video. Not a full video. Someone took the original video image, zoomed into it and cut out an area. Anomalous blurring – Oh, this mysterious and menacing “anomalous blurring”, which is simply seeing two fields of the same interlaced video frame (read about it on Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interlaced_video) in the resulting progressive video at the same time due to incorrect or poorly chosen deinterlacing settings. Happens a lot to amateur video editors.

The "frozen frames", if they actually exist (we have to take word of the "expert" for this"), may easily be an artifact of poor video processing. Not at all unusual. Transcoding irregularities. One likely reason is frame rate for the project being different from that of the imported video. Also buffer problems are possible, and multitude of other reasons. The “expert” says - “every second there are 30 separate images”, which is true only for American standard progressive video. The interlaced video, traditionally used for television, has “fields” not “frames”, at the double rate of the nominal frame rate. Thus an American standard interlaced video would have 60 fields (2x30), each capturing every other “scan line” of the image. European standard interlaced video would have 50 fields (2x25). This gives us at once technical explanation for two phenomena observed – the “blurring” and the “frozen frames”, both being artifacts of poor handling of interlaced video (blurring) with possibly a different frame rate (freezing).

It's a polished piece of art, but it's a damn functional one and I have yet to find anything better for the job. 21+1 .45 ACP 230gr Fiocchi XTP.

Concealed has been modernized to a few guns depending on wardrobe (for example a suit, or more loose-fitting clothes and/or winter wear), right now I alternate between a CZ 2075 RAMI 9mm 14+1 and a XD-E 45 7+1 for the conceal based on outside criteria. Both guns serve a similar purpose and have similar configurations - DA/SA, external manual safety+decocker combo for the hammer.

I should probably clarify I follow a pretty strict "right tool for the job" mentality with everything; from guns and animals to scotch. I'm a professional, although I would certainly not consider myself rich, so I have a bigger budget than some but can't afford a $30,000 pre-ban full auto H&K. My decisions are thus made upon what I consider a fair "medium" budget where I make choices to min/max, such as buying a CZ-97b for $600, and then sending it to Cajun for another $400 work-over to turn it into a gun that puts the highest end "single gunsmith" $3,000-$4,000 high-end luxury Wilson Combat or similar to absolute shame. This pistol is an absolute beast, and the wife (who can shoot far better than I, which is why she's guarding my six) can nail an 18" plate pretty damn consistently at 100 yards with this pistol, which I find pretty amazing.

This isn't to say the top-tier guns can not be worth the money for their purpose, and I personally own a Nighthawk and do not regret the decision, but only to stress that there are a significant amount of medium tier guns at $400-$600 prices that not only shine on their own merits, but also have readily available aftermarket shops which can turn them into $1,000-$1,200 guns that smoke their competition's offerings at three times the price. Not everyone will do the research necessary for this, which is probably a factor that's hard to really consider, but these types of options are on the table for everyone so they are definitely within reach for even someone on a very limited budget to save up for over a period of time.
